prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the checkout counter, payment terminal, and countertop very close to the camera wearer—roughly 0.3–0.8 m away—with the counter spanning the lower foreground and the terminal mainly on the left. The person across the counter is farther away, approximately 1–2 m, and shifts from partly visible near the upper centre/right in frames 1–4 to a larger, nearer figure on the right in frame 5, consistent with either her approaching or the wearer turning toward her. Darker regions behind her and above the counter indicate a background several metres away, while foreground objects partly occlude her lower body. This map makes near/far layering clearer than RGB, but its absolute metre estimates, clipped bright foreground, merged surfaces, and changing brightness across frames are unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates large foreground surfaces and people: a large mask labelled “laptop” occupies the left/lower foreground in frames 1–3, masks labelled “book” lie farther back and to the right, and person masks appear near the upper centre in frames 3–4 and prominently on the right in frame 5. Spatially, the large foreground mask is within the wearer’s arm’s reach, about 0.3–0.8 m away, while the person is across the counter at roughly 1–2 m; the labelled objects are generally between them or beside the person, so their mutual separations are approximately 0.5–1.5 m. Across the sequence, the viewpoint shifts right and the person changes from partial and upper-edge-occluded to much larger and more fully visible, while several foreground objects move out of frame. The masks expose object boundaries and occlusions that are difficult to follow in RGB, but labels such as “laptop,” “book,” and “tv” appear inconsistent with the checkout equipment and sign, small objects are missed, and mask shapes sometimes merge or truncate objects.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects no reliable body or hand landmarks in frames 1, 2, and 4, but shows a small partial skeleton near the upper-right of frame 3 and a much larger upper-body skeleton on the right in frame 5. The frame-3 figure is across the counter, roughly 1–2 m away and partly outside or occluded near the top edge; in frame 5 the larger skeleton indicates the person is nearer or more directly framed, approximately 1–1.5 m away, with head above shoulders and arms extending downward in front of the torso. The frame-5 shoulder geometry suggests the torso faces generally toward the camera wearer, but sparse facial points do not reliably establish gaze; no magenta hand skeletons are clearly visible, so hand reach and exact hand-object distances cannot be determined. Pose clarifies approximate body orientation and joint arrangement despite RGB blur, but the many missing frames, incomplete limbs, floating facial points, and absent hand detections make temporal motion and arm’s-reach judgments unreliable.
